parole.significato: The nation said to be descended from him, living mostly in the Negev and some later migrating to Israel.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew עֲמָלֵק (ʾĂmālēq).

parole.significato: A set of organisms descended from some originally created species (based on the Biblical doctrine of Special Creation);…
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew בָּרָא (bārāˀ, “he created”) + מיִן (mīʸn, “kind”) (misunderstood to mean "created kind"), coined by American creationist Frank Lewis Marsh in 1941.

parole.significato: To be buried together with one's forebears; hence, to die.

catena.traslitterazione: prosetéthē pròs toùs patéras autoû, Apocrypha

parole.testo: From various passages in the Bible, including Judges 2:10, and 1 Maccabees 2:69 in the Apocrypha (see the quotations), from From Biblical Hebrew נֶאֱסַף אֶל־אֲבוֹתָיו (neʾĕsap ʾel-ʾăḇôṯâw) and Koine Greek προσετέθη πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας αὐτοῦ (prosetéthē pròs toùs patéras autoû, Apocrypha).

parole.significato: A place or group in which people who have met failure or defeat in some way are said to congregate.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew מְעָרַת־עֲדֻלָּם (məʿāraṯ-ʿĂḏullām, “cave of Adullam”), referring to a redoubt near the town of Adullam where David fled from his enemy King Saul of Israel.

parole.significato: Any of various former units of volume
parole.testo: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew כֹּר (kōr).

parole.significato: A paradise on Earth.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew עֵדֶן (ʿḗḏen), perhaps from Sumerian 𒂔 (edin, “steppe, garden”).

parole.significato: A person from Ekron.
parole.testo: From Ekron + -ite, from Biblical Hebrew עֶקְרוֹן (ʿEqrōn).

parole.significato: A priestly vestment, without sleeves, worn girdled at the waist.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew אֵפֹד (ʼēp̄ōḏ).

parole.significato: The leader of the Jews of the Babylonian exile.
parole.testo: From exile + -arch, a calque of Biblical Hebrew רֹאשׁ גָּלוּת (rôš galûṯ).

parole.significato: The traditional punishments of Hell.
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew גׇּפְרִ֣ית וָאֵ֑שׁ (gofrit va’esh) and Ancient Greek πυρὸς καὶ θείου (puròs kaì theíou), appearing in both the Hebrew Bible and the New Testament. "brimstone" is an old word for sulfur.

parole.significato: An idyllic place wherein innocence and perfection reign; any delightful region or abode; a pastoral utopia; an Arcadia.
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew גַּן עֵדֶן (gan ʿḗḏen).

parole.significato: A musical term of uncertain meaning (possibly the name of an instrument), found in the Bible.
parole.testo: A transliteration of Biblical Hebrew גתית.

parole.significato: An exclamation used in songs of praise or thanksgiving to God.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Biblical Hebrew הַלְּלוּיָהּ (halləlūyɔh), from הַלְּלוּ (halləlū, “praise!”) + יָהּ (yɔh, “Lord, Jah”).

parole.significato: A person of the Hittite Kingdom, a Bronze Age kingdom of Anatolia.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew חִתִּי (ḥittî), from Hittite 𒄩𒋾 (ḫati), perhaps ultimately an exonym related to Hatti. In reference to the Indo-European-speaking people of Asia Minor (as opposed to the Biblical Hittites), this term was first used in the early 20th century in confusion with the neighboring Hatt

parole.significato: Hypocritically or self-righteously pious; sanctimonious; smugly morally superior.
parole.testo: From Isaiah 65:5 in the Bible (King James Version; spelling modernized): “Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou”; from Biblical Hebrew קְדַשְׁתִּיךָ (qəḏaštîḵā).

parole.significato: The most sacred place within a sacred building.
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew קודש הקודשים \ קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים (kódesh hakodashím).

parole.significato: Expressing regret at a loss of former glory or high standards.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew אִיכָבוֹד (ʾīḵāḇōḏ, literally “no honor”), from אִי (ʾī, “not”) + כָּבוֹד (kāḇōḏ, “honor”); alluding to 1 Samuel 4:21, where Eli’s daughter-in-law names her child Ichabod, saying ‘The glory is departed from Israel.’

parole.significato: A Jehovah's Witness.
parole.testo: Transliteration of Hebrew יְהֹוָה (yəhōwā), the Masoretic vocalization of the Biblical Hebrew יהוה (variously pronounced). The Masoretic vocalization is a so-called qere perpetuum, the deliberate insertion of the vowels of another word than the one represented by the consonant text, in this case אֲד

parole.significato: One whose chastity is above temptation.
parole.testo: From Middle English Ioseph, ultimately from Biblical Hebrew יוֹסֵף (Yoséf, literally “(God) shall add”); a son of Jacob. Doublet of Yusuf. Noun sense 1 (“one whose chastity is above temptation”) is a reference to the story of Joseph and Potiphar's wife in Genesis 39.

parole.significato: A Joshua tree.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Yehoshúa'), perhaps from הוֹשֵׁעַ (Hoshéa') with addition of יהוה (YHWH, “Yahweh”), thus meaning "Yahweh is salvation". See הוֹשִׁיעַ (hoshía', “to save”). By cognate a direct equivalent to Jesus via Latin Iēsūs and Ancient Greek Ἰησοῦς (Iēsoûs) from Aramaic יֵשׁוּע

parole.significato: An imaginary or real land of abundance, particularly the Land of Israel.
parole.testo: From English translations of Exodus 3:7-8. Calque of Biblical Hebrew אֶרֶץ זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ.

parole.significato: A flowering plant, Convallaria majalis, with richly fragrant pendant bells.
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew שׁוֹשַׁנַּת הָעֲמָקִים (šôšannat hāʿămāqîm), a reference to Song of Solomon 2:1.

parole.significato: Beelzebub; Satan
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew בַּעַל זְבוּב (baʿal zəḇûḇ, “fly-lord, Beelzebub”), which in turn is a mistranslation of the name of the Semitic devil Baal-zevuv.

parole.significato: A very large wine bottle (named after the King) with the capacity of about 15 liters, equivalent to 20 standard bottles.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Biblical Hebrew נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר (Nəḇûḵaḏneʾṣṣár), a corruption of earlier נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר (Nəḇûḵaḏreʾṣṣár), from Akkadian 𒀭𒀝𒃻𒁺𒋀 (Nabû-kudurri-uṣur, “Nabu protect my heir”).

parole.significato: A direction for the musical accompaniment of a psalm that has been interpreted as "stringed instruments".
parole.testo: Borrowed from Biblical Hebrew נְגִינוֹת (nəḡīnōṯ), plural of נְגִינָה (nəḡīnā, “playing of music on a stringed instrument”).

parole.significato: A former small Hebrew unit of dry volume equal to about 2.3 L or 2.1 quarts.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew עומר / עֹמֶר ('ómer, “sheaf”).

parole.significato: A large horned animal in ancient Hebrew literature, variously identified with the wild ox or aurochs (Bos primigenius),…
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew רְאֵם (r'em).

parole.significato: A flower of uncertain kind: perhaps Pancratium maritimum, which grows on the Sharon Plain of the coast of the Mediterra…
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew חֲבַצֶּלֶת הַשָּׁרוֹן (khavatsélet hasharón), from the King James Bible.

parole.significato: In the Mosaic Day of Atonement ritual, a goat symbolically imbued with the sins of the people, and sent out alive into…
parole.testo: From scape + goat; coined by English biblical scholar and translator William Tyndale, interpreting Biblical Hebrew עֲזָאזֵל (“azazél”) (Leviticus 16:8, 10, 26), from an interpretation as coming from עֵז (ez, “goat”) and אוזל (ozél, “escapes”). First attested 1530. Compare English scapegrace, scapega

parole.significato: A word occurring between verses or paragraphs in parts of the Hebrew Bible, namely in Habakkuk and the Psalms; perhaps…
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew סֶלָה (sélā), of unknown origin.

parole.significato: Synonym of salamander (“solidified material in a furnace hearth”).
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew שדרך (šdrk /⁠šadrak⁠/), from Iranian, ultimately from Proto-Iranian *čiθráh with the hypocoristic suffix *-akah.

parole.significato: A flapper (daring young woman of the Jazz Age).
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew שְׁבָא (Šəḇāʾ).

parole.significato: A particular pronunciation or custom that is regarded as distinguishing members of a group from non-members, especially…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Biblical Hebrew שִׁבֹּלֶת /שיבולת (šibbṓleṯ, “ear [of wheat] or stream, torrent”). Doublet of sebboleth and Middle English sebolech, both from Late Latin sebboleth in the Vulgate.

parole.significato: To be buried together with one's forebears; hence, to die; also, to be dead.
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew וַיִּשְׁכַּב עִם־אֲבֹתָיו (wayyiškaḇ ʿim-ʾăḇōṯâw, literally “he slept with his fathers”) (found, for example, in the Bible at 1 Kings 2:10); compare be gathered to one's fathers.

parole.significato: Chaos, disorder, confusion.
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ, from תֹּהוּ (tóhu, “nothingness, void”) + בֹּהוּ (bóhu, “emptiness, desolation”).

parole.significato: Certain sacred objects (whose precise form and nature is unknown) that were worn on the breastplate of the Jewish high…
parole.testo: From Biblical Hebrew אוּרִים (ʾûrîm) and תומים / תֻּמִּים (tummîm). Traditionally the Hebrew has been understood, and sometimes translated, as “Light and Truth” owing to the similarity to אוֹרִים (ʾôrîm, “lights”) and תָּמִים (tāmîm, “complete, morally upright, in accordance with truth”), an interpr

parole.significato: I, me
parole.testo: Calque of Biblical Hebrew עַבְדְּךָ (ʿaḇdəḵā) and עַבְדְּכֶם (ʿaḇdəḵem)

parole.significato: A place of refuge; a sanctuary.
parole.testo: From Zoar, mentioned in the Bible as the place where Lot fled with his wife and two daughters to escape death when Yahweh destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, from Biblical Hebrew צֹעַר (tso`ar, “insignificance, smallness”).

parole.significato: An exclamation of shock.
parole.testo: From Latin Mōsēs, from Ancient Greek Μωσῆς (Mōsês), from earlier Μωυσῆς (Mōusês), from Biblical Hebrew מֹשֶׁה (mōšê). Further etymology is unclear, but it is sometimes conjectured to derive from Egyptian ms-s (msj, “to give birth to”), a common element in Egyptian names of the form ‘[name of deity]
